topic.title: Agent Planning, Execution, and Reusable Experience
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: Tool-using agents must turn a goal into actions that remain useful as an environment responds. This topic studies long-horizon planning, execution coordination, memory, and reusable skills. A representative training framework generates plans and alternative trajectories, then gives greater weight to examples where the proposed plan and actual execution agree.
topic.whyItMatters: A plausible plan can fail through an impractical step, lost context, or deviation during execution. Evaluating agents across sessions and complex interfaces exposes these failures and tests whether stored experience improves future decisions rather than merely expanding memory.
topic.evolution: The representatives begin with goal-directed web navigation and working-memory structures. More recent papers introduce compositional workplace tasks, tool-oriented conversations, and planning–execution optimization. Experience-based approaches now distinguish action-level guidance from broader task skills and retrieve both using the current visual context.
openQuestions: How can agents recognize when a stored skill no longer fits the environment?
Which benchmarks measure durable improvement across tasks and sessions without rewarding memorized workflows?
